land.text: Derbent, the Caspian Gates city, an Abbasid frontier post under Arminiya

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Arminiya; Abbasid Caliphate'. The first Arab attack on Derbent was in 642 under Suraqa ibn Amr.

land.text: Derbent, absorbed into the Shirvanshah state after 1225

successors.note: The page gives the end as c. 1173 or c. 1225; the Ilkhanate set a commander of the march of Derbent in 1265.

capitals.name: Derbent (Darband, Bab al-Abwab)
capitals.note: The emirate was the city of Derbent and its pass; the page gives no extent.

rulers.name: Hashim b. Suraqa
rulers.title: emir
rulers.note: The page's 'selected rulers': there are large gaps (Hashimids to 1075, then the Aghlabid line and a later dynasty that Abu Hamid al-Gharnati knew c. 1130-1150; 1154-1164, c. 1173, c. 1180-c. 1222 and c. 1222-c. 1225 are 'c.' dates).

rulers.name: Mansur II b. Abd al-Malik II
rulers.title: emir

correction.text: Derbent and its pass, the Hashimid emirate

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 869-1074. The page gives no extent or area, so a 40 km circle round Derbent (the reading the Shirvan dossier uses for its c. 1201 gain) stands for the city and its pass.

New keyframe, 1130-1225. Same circle. The page shows emirs again from the Aghlabid line and a later dynasty (Muzaffar c. 1154-1164 to Rashid c. 1222-c. 1225); the restoration year after 1075 is not on the page, and 1075-1129 is drawn as Shirvanshah land.

ledger.note: 869: the emirate of Derbent is formed. 'The autonomous or independent emirate was formed in 869 by Hashim b. Suraqa b. Salis b. Hayyun' (infobox 'Established: c. 869'), ending Abbasid governors' rule at the Caspian Gates.

1075: Fariburz I of Shirvan annexes Derbent. 'The Hashimid dynasty fell from power in 1075 when Fariburz I annexed Derbent'; Maymun II b. Mansur II ruled only from 20 August to December 1075. [Reviewer eu-19-x, 2026-10-31: month 8 removed: the page gives no month for the annexation and its rulers table has Maymun II reigning 20 August-December 1075, so August cannot be the end.]

c. 1130: Derbent is back under its own emirs. The page does not date the restoration after 1075: it says Seljuk intervention led to the Aghlabid line (Aghlab b. Ali appointed by Savtegin) and lists a later dynasty known to Abu Hamid al-Gharnati in the period c. 1130-1150; the year is a bridge.

region.text: Derbent, taken into the Shirvanshah state

ledger.note: c. 1225: the emirate ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 1173 or c. 1225'; Rashid b. Farrukhzad was the last emir (c. 1222-c. 1225) and 'The emirate was again absorbed into Shirvanshah state after 1225'. The Shirvan dossier dates the Shirvanshah take-over c. 1201 from its own page.

wars.name: Khazar raid on Derbent
wars.outcome: 'In 901 AD (288 AH), the Emirate faced a large-scale Khazar raid.' The Hashimid emirs fought the Khazars, Rus' and Sarir repeatedly; no border change is given.

wars.name: Fariburz I's annexation of Derbent
wars.outcome: Fariburz I of Shirvan annexed Derbent in 1075 and the Hashimid dynasty fell.

wars.name: Georgian defeat of Emir Bek-Bars
wars.outcome: 'Akhsitan I, with his cousin George III (r. 1156-1184), defeated emir Bek-Bars b. Muzaffar around 1173'; no land change is given.

certainty.note: A city and its pass: no frontier on the page, drawn as a soft 40 km circle.

sources.title: Emirate of Derbent
sources.note: Founding 869, Hashimid rulers, 1075 annexation, c. 1173/c. 1225 end; no extent, no area.

notes: No Cliopatria row. The Shirvan dossier (eu-19-c) has a gain c. 1201 with counterpart 'Maliks of Darband' from the Shirvan page; this page has the emirate fall to Fariburz I in 1075, be restored under another line, and be absorbed 'after 1225'; the counterpart string should read emirate-of-derbent. The infobox end is 'c. 1173 or c. 1225'; 1225 is used because the last listed emir rules to c. 1225. The 1130 restoration is a confidence-1 bridge. Extent is a 40 km circle round Derbent because no page gives a frontier. wikidata null. Not opened (page budget): Derbent, Hashimid dynasty and Aghlabid dynasty pages; a gap-filler could date the restoration after 1075 there.
